name: claude-dashboard
description: Unofficial. A 23-tab dashboard over every Claude Code transcript on the machine — spend, agents, workflows, limits — and a configurable status bar for the numbers you want in front of you.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Reads only Claude Code's own state under the home directory; nothing from the workspace is executed or trusted.

virtualWorkspaces.description: No workspace file is ever read; the workspace path is used only to match Claude sessions of this repository, and in a virtual workspace that match finds nothing.

commands.title: Claude: Export usage as CSV or JSON
Claude: Copy the workflow run id

claudeStatusline.segments.markdownDescription:
One status-bar item per string, left to right. Write literal text, `{placeholders}`, and `[optional groups]` that vanish whole when a placeholder inside them has nothing to say. A segment whose placeholders are all empty hides itself.

Run **Claude Statusline: List status-bar placeholders** to see every name with the value it has right now.

Limits: `{weekly}` `{weeklyBar}` `{plan}` `{drift}` `{dry}` `{dryAt}` `{dryLeft}` `{reset}` `{resetLeft}` `{session5h}` `{session5hLeft}` `{scoped}` `{scoped:Opus}`

Session: `{ctx}` `{ctxTokens}` `{ctxWindow}` `{ctxCache}` `{compact}` `{model}` `{effort}` `{advisor}` `{thinking}` `{outputStyle}` `{branch}` `{version}` `{update}`

Spend: `{cost}` `{burn}` `{today}` `{requests}` `{duration}` `{apiShare}` `{added}` `{removed}`

Work: `{peers}` `{peersBusy}` `{todo}` `{todoActive}` `{jobs}` `{sessions}` `{openTasks}`

Workflow: `{wfName}` `{wfAgents}` `{wfElapsed}` `{wfCost}` `{wfRuns}`

VS Code icons work too: `$(flame)`, `$(rocket)`. A backslash escapes `{`, `}`, `[` and `]`.

claudeStatusline.fetchLimits.markdownDescription:
Ask Anthropic for the account's limits.

When on, the extension reads the OAuth token Claude Code already stores (macOS Keychain, falling back to `~/.claude/.credentials.json`) and sends it in one `Authorization` header to `https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage` — the same endpoint `/usage` reads. The answer is cached in `~/.claude/statusline-usage.json`, shared with `statusline.sh`, at most once a minute per machine. The token is not stored, copied or sent anywhere else.

When off, nothing leaves the machine and the token is never read. Limit fields then come from that cache if something else wrote it, and stay empty otherwise; everything drawn from local transcripts — context, spend, workflows, the dashboard — is unaffected.

claudeStatusline.autoRefresh.markdownDescription:
Redraw the dashboard and the status bar on a timer.

On, both refresh every `claudeStatusline.refreshInterval` seconds. Off, the status bar still updates from the cheap ten-second read, but the expensive pass — the full transcript index, the spend across every project, the limits request — happens only when you ask for it with **Reindex** or **Claude: Refresh now**.

Turn it off on battery, or while a page is open that you want to keep still.

claudeStatusline.monthlyBudget.markdownDescription:
A spend ceiling for the calendar month, in dollars.

Set it above zero and the dashboard draws the month against it and the extension says so once at 80% and once at 100% — once per month each, not on every tick. Zero turns both off.

The figure is an estimate from public per-million-token rates across every transcript on this machine, not a bill.

claudeStatusline.fetchChangelog.markdownDescription:
Fetch the full Claude Code changelog.

**Off by default.** With it off, the Changelog tab reads the copy the client already keeps in `~/.claude/cache/changelog.md` — which covers the version running and a little history, and lags a release by up to a day.

With it on, the extension fetches `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/claude-code/main/CHANGELOG.md` — one public file, no credentials, at most once an hour — and shows every release Anthropic has published. The answer is cached in the extension's own storage.

claudeStatusline.checkPluginUpdates.markdownDescription:
Ask each plugin's marketplace whether a newer version exists.

**Off by default, and off means nothing leaves the machine.** With it off the Health tab still lists every installed plugin, its version and what actually ran — it simply cannot tell you which of them is out of date, because that answer only exists on a server.

With it on, the extension fetches the marketplace manifest each plugin was installed from, at most once an hour, and compares versions. No credentials are sent and nothing about your usage is transmitted — only a request for a public manifest.

claudeStatusline.refreshInterval.description: How often to refresh limits and session stats, in seconds.

claudeStatusline.alignment.description: Which side of the status bar to use. Applied immediately.

claudeStatusline.priority.description: Priority within the chosen side: higher means further left. Applied immediately.
